reports.title: CON EDISON REPORTS 2026 THIRD QUARTER EARNINGS

lines: For the year of 2026, Con Edison expects its adjusted earnings per share (non-GAAP) to be in the range of $6.05 to $6.15 per share.

3Q 2026 Financial Highlights $2.07 earnings per share (GAAP) / $2.07 adjusted earnings per share (non-GAAP)(a) Narrowed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance range $6.05 to $6.15 adjusted earnings per share (non- GAAP)(a) CECONY entered into a joint proposal for the Steam rate plan - reflects 9.50% ROE, 48% equity ratio(b) 4 (a) Adjusted EPS is a non-GAAP financial measure.

Excludes the Utilities' average interest bearing Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) of approximately $2.6 billion at year-end 2025, with annual average balances expected to range between approximately $2.1 billion and $3.9 billion from 2026 - 2030. b.

(page 53) In October 2026, CECONY updated its five-year forecast of average annual summer peak electric demand in its service area at design conditions from a 0.7 percent increase (for 2026 to 2030) to a 0.8 percent increase (for 2027 to 2031).

(page 53) In October 2026, O&R updated its five-year forecast of average annual summer peak electric demand in its service area at design conditions from a 4.1 percent increase (for 2026 to 2030) to a 2.6 percent increase (for 2027 to 2031).

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS up 9% to $2.07, in line; 2026 earnings range narrowed to $6.05–6.15
results: Net income rose to $766m ($2.07 a share) from $688m; adjusted EPS rose to $2.07 from $1.90.
Growth came mainly from a bigger electric rate base at the New York City utility (CECONY), adding 17c a share.
New share issuance diluted EPS by 5c; about $216m was raised through the share-sale programme by September.
For nine months, adjusted EPS was $5.08 versus $4.82; reported EPS of $5.44 includes a gain on selling the Mountain Valley Pipeline stake.
A settlement on a new three-year steam rate plan (9.5% return on equity) awaits regulator approval.

guidance.summary: Con Edison tightened its 2026 adjusted EPS forecast to $6.05–6.15 from $6.00–6.20, keeping the same midpoint.

points: Management stressed electrification-driven demand growth in New York and plans about $797m of climate-resilience spending in 2026–2030.
The CFO highlighted the agreement reached on the new steam rate plan as a sign of a workable regulatory relationship.
The investor slides project average rate base growing about 8.7% a year over five years.
Customer affordability was a major theme, as was New York's new Chapter 58 law on rate cases, whose impact is still being assessed.
call.source: Earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2) and executive comments in the press release; no call coverage found

watch: Regulator decision on the steam rate plan (sessions on 19 Nov and 17 Dec 2026).
How Chapter 58 affects the timing and terms of future rate cases from 2027.
Further share issuance under the $2bn programme and its effect on EPS.
